items.title: Reverse proxy: server ka front door, aur load balancer se fark
items.one_idea: A reverse proxy is a server that sits in front of your servers: clients talk only to it, it forwards each request to a backend server and returns the response; that one front door can balance load, terminate TLS, cache and compress, hides the backend servers, and is also a single point of failure. A forward proxy is the opposite side: it sits in front of clients. A load balancer is one job a reverse proxy can do.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: reverse proxy और load balancer में क्या फर्क है?
keywords: forward proxy vs reverse proxy hindi
items.hook_formula: interviewer_asked: one complete real interview question; the answer starts on the next line (reverse proxy is the front door, load balancer is one of its jobs). No staged pause.
items.visual_idea: One fixed frame: client icons on the left, one door-shaped box in the middle, three server boxes on the right behind it with no direct lines from clients. A request enters the door and leaves to one server; the response returns through the door. Then job tags (balance, TLS, cache, compress) light up one by one on the door; last, the door itself gets a red cross to show it can go down. A small mirrored sketch shows the forward proxy on the client side.
items.everyday_anchor: A hotel reception desk: guests never walk to the rooms, the desk takes the request and sends it to the right room.
items.example: EXAMPLE: clients ask for /app and /static; the proxy sends /app to server group A and serves /static from its cache. Paths and groups invented.
facts_to_verify: Wikipedia: reverse proxy appears to clients as an ordinary web server and forwards to backends; listed uses load balancing, TLS termination, caching, compression, security, hiding origin servers; it can be a single point of failure
MDN: forward proxies can hide client identities, reverse proxies can hide server identities; X-Forwarded-For carries the original client IP

NGINX guide: proxy_pass forwards a request to a proxied server; 'A common use of a reverse proxy is to provide load balancing'; responses are buffered by default; Host header is reset unless proxy_set_header sets it
avoid_claims: reverse proxy makes things faster by a number
nginx handles N requests per second
